newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS BEAT RANGERS TO TAKE 2-1 LEAD IN EASTERN FINALS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS BEAT RANGERS TO TAKE 2-1 LEAD IN EASTERN FINALS.

text.p: Trent Klatt scored the go-ahead goal off a 2-on-1 with 5:01 left and Eric Lindros posted his first playoff hat trick as the Philadelphia Flyers beat the New York Rangers 6-3 Tuesday to take a 2-1 lead in the Eastern Conference finals.
Philadelphia blew a two-goal lead but scored three times in the final 5:01 to regain home-ice advantage in the best-of-seven series. Game Four is Friday at New York.
The Rangers took advantage of a miscue by rookie defenceman Janne Niinimaa and rallied for a 3-3 tie with 5:39 to play on Wayne Gretzky's 10th playoff goal.

But New York defenceman Bruce Driver gambled in the neutral zone and was trapped as Klatt and Shjon Podein broke in 2-on-1. Klatt worked a give-and-go before wristing a shot between the pads of sliding goaltender Mike Richter.
Less than two minutes later, with the Rangers throwing all five players into the attack, Rod Brind'Amour beat Richter on a breakaway to make it 5-3.
Lindros, limited to two shots over the first two games of the series, scored into an empty net with 38 seconds remaining to complete his hat trick.
Ron Hextall made 25 saves in his second postseason start for Philadelphia.
